sample_unit: consecutive metastatic prostate cancer cases (each evaluated with five LLMs)
models_evaluated: Five contemporary LLMs accessed via public web interfaces (names not given in the text)

links.outcome: Proportion of LLM treatment-planning outputs passing MDT one-strike safety adjudication
links.effect: Safety rates ranged from 79.0% to 84.9%; about 15%-21% of outputs breached safety thresholds under a strict gate, precluding unsupervised use.
links.quote: Current LLMs can support mPCa care as drafting assistants, but ∼15%-21% of outputs breached safety thresholds under a strict gate, precluding unsupervised use at initial treatment-planning encounters.

links.outcome: Clinically unsafe LLM outputs identified by expert multidisciplinary review of real patient cases
links.effect: Safety rates 79.0%-84.9%; failures clustered in hard cases with incomplete documentation (missingness-related extraction errors, disease-state/pathway errors, guideline logic deviations, safety-check omissions).
links.quote: Failures clustered in hard cases with incomplete documentation and were dominated by missingness-related extraction errors, disease-state/pathway errors, guideline logic deviations, and safety-check omissions.

screen.reason: Multicenter retrospective expert evaluation of 5 commercial LLMs for clinical decision support in metastatic prostate cancer, evaluating safety rates and expert ratings without testing a specific deployment intervention.
